entities.name: Dorothea Brooke
entities.description: Eager to devote her life to something worthwhile, Dorothea looks for a purpose larger than the comfortable future expected of her.

entities.name: Celia Brooke
entities.description: Practical and attentive to ordinary pleasures, Celia often sees what her sister’s ideals obscure.

entities.name: Edward Casaubon
entities.description: A clergyman absorbed in an ambitious scholarly project, Casaubon hopes to give his work lasting authority.

entities.name: Tertius Lydgate
entities.description: Lydgate brings scientific ambitions and plans for medical reform into a town where patronage and reputation shape professional life.

entities.name: Rosamond Vincy
entities.description: Accomplished and socially ambitious, Rosamond imagines a future of refinement beyond the limits of her familiar circle.

entities.name: Fred Vincy
entities.description: Affectionate but unreliable, Fred hopes luck and inheritance will spare him difficult decisions about work.

entities.name: Mary Garth
entities.description: Mary’s wit and self-respect make her unwilling to confuse affection with excuses for bad conduct.

entities.name: Caleb Garth
entities.description: Caleb values skilled work and honest dealings. His devotion to useful labor offers a different measure of success from money or status.

entities.name: Will Ladislaw
entities.description: Independent in outlook and uncertain of his vocation, Will resists the paths other people prescribe for him.

entities.name: Nicholas Bulstrode
entities.description: Bulstrode’s wealth supports local institutions, giving his religious convictions considerable public influence.

entities.name: Harriet Bulstrode
entities.description: Born into the Vincy family, Harriet combines social pride with warmth and loyalty.

entities.name: Camden Farebrother
entities.description: Humane and alert to his own weaknesses, Farebrother offers friendship without demanding that people be flawless.

entities.name: Sir James Chettam
entities.description: Well-meaning and attentive to practical improvements, Sir James takes an active interest in the Brooke sisters.

additionalEntities.name: John Raffles
additionalEntities.description: A man with connections to Bulstrode’s earlier life. Reveal further detail only after the reader reaches the relevant disclosures.

additionalEntities.name: Peter Featherstone
additionalEntities.description: An elderly property owner whose relations and dependents watch his intentions closely.

additionalEntities.name: Mr. Brooke
additionalEntities.description: Dorothea and Celia’s uncle, a landowner with wide interests and uncertain follow-through.

additionalEntities.name: Susan Garth
additionalEntities.description: Caleb’s wife, whose practical judgment supports their household.

identityDecisions: Dorothea Brooke and Mrs. Casaubon are one person; Edward Casaubon is a separate entity. Do not let surname-only matches swallow the wife’s married name.
Celia Brooke and Lady Chettam are one person; Sir James Chettam is separate. Married aliases require source-position review before exposing relationships.
Rosamond Vincy and Mrs. Lydgate are one person; Tertius Lydgate is separate.
Nicholas and Harriet Bulstrode require separate records. The plural Bulstrodes denotes the household, not a single person.
Fred, Rosamond, Mr. Vincy, and Mrs. Vincy must not be merged by surname.
Caleb, Susan, Mary, and the other Garth children must remain distinct. Do not use Garth alone as a universal alias.
Raffles and Joshua Rigg are distinct; reveal their family connection only at the appropriate reading position.
Use context-sensitive matching for Will, Mary, and generic titles such as the Vicar; no unqualified global matches.
integrationRequirements: Generate production character data only after all session parts are assembled and accepted.
Derive paragraph hashes and occurrence anchors from the exact accepted edition; this proposal makes no claim to runtime compatibility.
Keep introductory cards free of later outcomes. Unlock relationships and event summaries using verified source positions.
Review all aliases against the complete original and assembled modern edition, including characters introduced outside session mm-f.
